notice: Private research vocabulary for issue #1972. This is not a persisted schema or public SDK contract.

scenarios.oracle: A guest write is visible in the mounted host workspace.
scenarios.purpose: Prove the intended writable workspace boundary.

scenarios.oracle: A host marker outside every mount remains absent.
scenarios.purpose: Prove that guest writes cannot escape the declared workspace.

scenarios.oracle: Reads succeed and a mutation leaves the host fixture unchanged.
scenarios.purpose: Measure read-only mount support without assuming parity.

scenarios.oracle: Synthetic host credential material cannot be read by the guest.
scenarios.purpose: Keep host credential storage outside the guest filesystem.

scenarios.oracle: Symlink and parent traversal attempts leave the outside marker absent.
scenarios.purpose: Exercise common path-confusion escape techniques.

scenarios.oracle: Scoped temporary artifacts are removed and teardown is idempotent.
scenarios.purpose: Prove probe cleanup rather than assuming process exit is sufficient.

scenarios.oracle: An unlisted TCP destination receives no connection.
scenarios.purpose: Establish the backend default-deny baseline.

scenarios.oracle: Only the adapter-bound allowed fixture receives the request.
scenarios.purpose: Prove the narrow positive egress path.

scenarios.oracle: The adjacent hostname receives no request.
scenarios.purpose: Measure hostname fidelity.

scenarios.oracle: The adjacent port receives no request.
scenarios.purpose: Measure port fidelity independently from hostname fidelity.

scenarios.oracle: A protocol outside the requested origin cannot reach a credentialed fixture.
scenarios.purpose: Distinguish TCP, host-port, and HTTP-origin enforcement.

scenarios.oracle: A redirect to the adjacent origin receives no credential and no successful request.
scenarios.purpose: Check whether policy is re-evaluated after redirects.

scenarios.oracle: Loopback/private destinations require an explicit adapter binding.
scenarios.purpose: Keep internal address access visible in effective policy.

scenarios.oracle: A controlled hostname resolution change is either blocked or explicitly unsupported.
scenarios.purpose: Record rebinding assurance without using a public rebinding service.

scenarios.oracle: Evidence contains both requested destinations and the full effective backend policy.
scenarios.purpose: Expose mandatory platform egress and fidelity reductions.

scenarios.oracle: Launch is not attempted when a required trusted binding is missing.
scenarios.purpose: Fail before guest startup when credential requirements cannot be satisfied.

scenarios.oracle: The guest sees a stand-in and the allowed origin sees the synthetic value.
scenarios.purpose: Prove host-side credential substitution.

scenarios.oracle: Wrong host and wrong port record zero synthetic credential matches.
scenarios.purpose: Prove that an allowed network path does not imply credential authority.

scenarios.oracle: Only the rotated synthetic value is accepted after rotation.
scenarios.purpose: Measure live credential rotation semantics.

scenarios.oracle: No synthetic value is delivered after revocation.
scenarios.purpose: Measure live revocation semantics.

scenarios.oracle: Restart semantics explicitly show whether trusted bindings persist or must be rebound.
scenarios.purpose: Separate durable guest state from host credential authority.

scenarios.oracle: The persistence sanitizer rejects every synthetic value and host path.
scenarios.purpose: Prevent probe evidence from becoming an exfiltration channel.

scenarios.oracle: A detached child delayed marker remains absent through the configured observation window after containment termination.
scenarios.purpose: Prove timeout kills the workload rather than only rejecting the host call.

scenarios.oracle: An explicitly cancelled detached child leaves no delayed marker.
scenarios.purpose: Prove cancellation reaches the containment boundary.

scenarios.oracle: An unavailable required broker prevents launch or request delivery.
scenarios.purpose: Record failed-open versus failed-closed behavior.

scenarios.oracle: A launch failure after resource creation leaves no backend residue.
scenarios.purpose: Exercise cleanup between allocation and usable handle return.

scenarios.oracle: Calling close twice succeeds and leaves no additional mutation.
scenarios.purpose: Make teardown safe for nested failure paths.

scenarios.oracle: Evidence distinguishes disk, process, tmpfs, VFS, and binding persistence.
scenarios.purpose: Characterize backend lifecycle semantics without normalizing them.

scenarios.oracle: The guest reports one online CPU when one CPU is requested.
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether CPU requests are independently observable.

scenarios.oracle: Guest memory is within fifteen percent of the requested 1 GiB.
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether memory requests are independently observable.

scenarios.oracle: MCP, host exec, signing, credential brokering, and model traffic are recorded outside guest containment.
scenarios.purpose: Prevent host capabilities from being misreported as sandbox controls.
